'''Taracad  Narayanan  Ananthakrishnan''' (15 December 1925 – 7 August 2015) was an Indian entomologist and insect ecologist. His areas of specialization was in the study of gall insects (Cecidology) and chemical ecology. He did extensive study of Indian thrips ([[Thysanoptera]]) and made immense contributions to this field of science.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.thehindu.com/2005/12/05/stories/2005120517670800.htm|work=[[The Hindu]]|title=Entomologist Hailed|date=2005-12-05|access-date=2017-02-26}}{{dead link|date=September 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Ananathakrishnan, a native of Taracad in [[Palakkad district]], [[Kerala]], was the eldest son of T. K. Narayanan and T. A. Annapurani. After completing schooling at Mangalore and Palghat, he completed undergraduate study in zoology at the [[Madras Christian College]], Madras (now Chennai) with honours in 1946.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Raman|first=Ananthanarayanan|year=2014|title=T.N.Ananthakrishnan, Living Legends in Science|url=http://www.currentscience.ac.in/Volumes/106/05/0749.pdf|journal=Current Science|volume=106}}</ref> He completed M.Sc. by research, obtained a Ph.D. followed by a D.Sc., all from the University of Madras.<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
Ananthakrishnan started his teaching career in Madras Christian College and was a lecturer in zoology there until 1948 before moving to [[Loyola College, Chennai|Loyola College]], Madras. At Loyola, he was a lecturer in zoology and was the Head of Department of Zoology until 1968 when he took up position as the founder director of the Entomology Research Institute<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.loyolacollege.edu/eri/aboutus.php|title=About Entomology Research Institute|access-date=26 February 2017|archive-date=21 November 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191121013050/http://www.loyolacollege.edu/eri/aboutus.php|url-status=dead}}</ref> that functions within the Loyola College campus at Chennai. He took up the position of director of [[Zoological Survey of India]] in 1977<ref name=":0" /> and served for five years.

He was greatly influenced by the Indian entomologist [[M. S. Mani (entomologist)|M. S. Mani]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.frontline.in/navigation/?type=static&page=flonnet&rdurl=fl1506/15061020.htm|title=Naturalists of India|website=Frontline|access-date=2017-03-05}}</ref> and M.Ekambaranathan (retired professor of zoology, Presidency College, Madras). He was inspired to study insects by [[T. V. Ramakrishna Ayyar]] and [[Yelsetti Ramachandra Rao|Y. Ramachandra Rao]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last=Raman|first=Ananthanarayanan|year=2015|title=T.N.Ananthakrishnan, Personal News|url=http://www.currentscience.ac.in/Volumes/109/05/0981.pdf|journal=Current Science|volume=109}}</ref> Being one of the early recipients of support from [[PL 480|PL-480]], he dedicated nearly three decades in the study and research of Indian thrips.

From the late 1990s onwards, every year he conducted a meeting to discuss on the subject of entomology<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.currentscience.ac.in/Downloads/article_id_097_03_0300_0301_0.pdf|title=Meeting Report|website=Current Science|access-date=2017-03-05}}</ref> in Chennai.

== Publications ==
Ananthakrishnan authored and co-authored numerous books on thrips.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.google.com/search?tbs=bks:1&q=%22T.N.+Ananthakrishnan%22|title="T.N. Ananthakrishnan" - Google Search|website=www.google.com|language=en|access-date=2017-03-04}}</ref> He published numerous research articles in Current Science, Bulletin of Entomology, Journal of Zoological Survey of India, Annual Review of Entomology, Journal of Scientific and Industrial Research, Indian Journal of Plant Protection and several others<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" />

== Awards ==
Ananthakrishnan was a Fellow of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]], Indian Natural Science Academy and the [[National Academy of Agricultural Sciences]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Ananthakrishnan,_Prof._Taracad_Narayanan|title=Fellow Profile|website=Indian Academy of Sciences|access-date=2017-02-26}}</ref> He was awarded the Dr K.V. Mehta Memorial Award in the year 1998<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.tribuneindia.com/1998/98dec31/nation.htm|title=Award for PAU Farm Scientist|date=31 December 1998}}</ref> and J.C. Bose Memorial award in 2000.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.thehindu.com/2000/01/04/stories/0204000m.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181002012350/https://www.thehindu.com/2000/01/04/stories/0204000m.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=2018-10-02|website=[[The Hindu]]|title=PM presents awards to 21 scientists|date=2000-01-04|access-date=2017-03-05}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Ananthakrishnan married Menaka of Taracad in 1950 and they have two children, Ranee and Ramdas. He was an ardent cricket fan and captained the Loyola College Academic and General Staff cricketing team.<ref name=":0" /> He died in New Jersey on 7 August 2015.{{citation needed|date=August 2017}}

== Influences ==
Fellow thysanopterists from India and overseas have named several new species of thrips after him.<ref name=":0" /> G.S. Gill Research Institute awards the Prof T. N. Ananthakrishnan Foundation award every year to one young Indian entomologist to recognize his/her contributions in the field of Entomology for their work done in India.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.associationofentomologists.com/awards.php|title=Welcome to Association of Entomologists|last=Entomologists|first=Association of|website=www.associationofentomologists.com|language=en|access-date=2017-03-05}}</ref>
